title: Lit environments that promote health and well-being
research_question: What are the photometric and colorimetric characteristics of the light field to which people are routinely exposed? Can Circadian Stimulus (CS) characterise such lighting settings?

participants.description: Nine real-world locations in and around London, chosen to be representative of urban and architectural lit environments where typical users (office workers, retail staff, outdoor workers) would routinely spend long periods of time. Settings included: Landscape, Square, Toplit Study space, Domestic Living room, Retail Bookshop, Office 1, Office 2a, Office 2b, Healthcare.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Nine real-world locations in and around London, measured under two sky conditions: overcast (8/8 okta) and sunny (2-3/8 oktas). Measurements were taken between approximately 11:00 a.m. and 1:00 p.m. during June 2019.

findings.antecedent: Lit environment type (deep open plan office, basement hospital reception)
findings.mechanism: Insufficient light exposure for non-image forming photoreceptors.
findings.quote: deep open plan office setting (Office 2a and 2b)... and the basement hospital reception (Healthcare), receive far less than 0.3 Circadian Stimulus

findings.antecedent: Lit environment type (natural vs. artificial/synthetic settings)
findings.mechanism: Natural environments provide light characteristics more aligned with evolved human circadian systems.
findings.quote: Generally as we move from more natural settings to more artificial/synthetic settings (i.e. from left to right) the CS potential decreases.

findings.antecedent: Lit environment type (study space with substantial daylight component, Top-lit)
findings.mechanism: High daylight levels contribute to effective circadian entrainment.
findings.quote: in both the overcast and sunny settings there is a substantial daylight component in the study space (Top-lit) arrangement, providing close to the maximum Circadian Stimulus of 0.7.

findings.antecedent: Lit environment type (single occupancy office with large windows, bookshop)
findings.mechanism: Generous side-lit conditions provide sufficient light for circadian stimulation.
findings.quote: Settings with large windows providing generous side lit conditions, such as the single occupancy office (Office 1) and the bookshop, provide at least CS = 0.3.

findings.antecedent: Exterior sun shading (awning) in retail bookshop
findings.consequent: Circadian Stimulus (CS) value on a sunny day
findings.mechanism: Reduced daylight ingress due to shading lowers circadian light exposure.
findings.quote: the bookshop (Retail) generates a low CS value on a sunny day-this is because the staff have chosen to install an awning to provide exterior sun shading.

findings.antecedent: Lit environment type (single occupancy office, Office 1)
findings.mechanism: High levels of inter-reflected light from large side windows and light-coloured walls contribute to a balanced light distribution and overall impression of lightness.
findings.quote: the highest ratio of vertical to horizontal illuminance is seen in the single occupancy office (Office 1) during both the sunny and overcast conditions.

findings.antecedent: Lit environment type (deep open plan office, Office 2a and 2b) with overhead downlights
findings.mechanism: Overhead lighting creates a less comfortable visual environment due to disproportionate light distribution.
findings.quote: The Ev/EH ratio in the deep open plan office (Office 2a and 2b) is fairly low during both sunny and overcast conditions especially when the overhead downlights are switched on, suggesting a less comfortable visual environment.

findings.mechanism: Extensive sky dome provides high ambient light levels.
findings.quote: the exterior settings achieve substantially higher cylindrical illuminance ratings than any of the interior environments

findings.antecedent: Lit environment type (top lit interior spaces)
findings.mechanism: Top-lighting contributes to higher ambient light levels compared to other interior settings.
findings.quote: Of all the interior settings, the top lit spaces perform best, although at a markedley lower level than the exterior settings

findings.antecedent: Lit environment type (domestic setting with fully glazed wall and large glazed rooflight)
findings.mechanism: Combination of high daylight levels and light-coloured wall finishes provides good inter-reflection and uniform three-dimensional illuminance.
findings.quote: The domestic setting performs better than the top lit space during the overcast conditions with this metric and this may be explained by the presence of the fully glazed wall together with the large glazed roof.

findings.antecedent: Lit environment type (natural and top-lit settings)
findings.mechanism: High Eeye leads to a light-adapted visual system, which is characteristic of natural environments.
findings.quote: The striking feature of these results is that the natural and top-lit settings produce high illuminance at the eye leading to a light-adapted visual system

findings.antecedent: Lit environment type (architectural settings: Office 1, 2a, 2b, Healthcare)
findings.mechanism: Architectural settings often provide lower corneal illuminance compared to natural environments.
findings.quote: reduces to a plateau as you move to more architectural settings (Office 1, 2a, 2b and Healthcare).

findings.antecedent: Lit environment type (high levels of daylight)
findings.consequent: Circadian Stimulus (CS) and mean cylindrical illuminance (Ec)
findings.mechanism: Environments with high daylight support non-image forming and visual functioning.
findings.quote: CS and mean cylindrical illuminance (Ec) seem to be running roughly in tandem and show generally that those environments with high levels of daylight score highly in both metrics

findings.consequent: Utility for characterizing health and well-being promoting environments
findings.mechanism: Ev/Eh is highly dependent on specific architectural geometries, making it less universally useful than CS for general health/well-being characterization.
findings.quote: These findings are in contrast with those seen in the ratio of vertical to horizontal illuminance (Ev/Eh), where higher values are the consequence of very specific architectural geometries. This metric may not be so useful in characterising lit environments that promote health and well-being.

findings.antecedent: Illumination metric (Illuminance at the eye, Eeye)
findings.consequent: Description of difference between natural and architectural environments
findings.mechanism: Eeye powerfully captures the distinct light exposure patterns of natural vs. built settings.
findings.quote: The illuminance at the eye (Eeye) powerfully describes the difference between natural and open urban environments compared to architectural interiors.

mechanisms: Light acts on non-image forming processes, impacting health and wellbeing via the circadian system, arousal system, and affective system.
Light signals reach the SCN (suprachiasmatic nuclei) via the retinohypothalamic tract, influencing endogenous circadian rhythms.
Melatonin production by the pineal gland is regulated by light, conveying time-of-day messages and influencing sleep-wake cycles, growth, puberty, and cancer development.
Intrinsically photoreceptive Retinal Ganglion Cells (ipRGCs), rods, and cones are involved in both visual and non-image forming phototransduction.
Melanopsin (in ipRGCs) is most sensitive to blue light (480nm), influencing melatonin suppression and alertness.
Red light (630nm) can also increase alertness, potentially via cone receptors sensitive to long wavelength light, suggesting involvement of neural pathways beyond melatonin suppression.
Serotonin, a precursor to melatonin, originates in the brainstem and projects to limbic structures, regulating mood, appetite, sleep, and overall wellness, with levels influenced by bright sunlight.
The human visual system evolved to process images from nature, suggesting a primacy of natural daylit environments for optimal functioning and comfort.
implementation_implications: More natural lit environments are expected to be beneficial for health and well-being.

It is important to consider the characteristics of the entire light field (spectral composition, intensity, light distribution) rather than just the light source when making recommendations for optimal illumination.
Application of full spectrum lighting (daylight) is preferred as it satisfies known mechanisms without adversely impacting others.
Excluding certain wavelengths of light (e.g., blue light) when considering optimal illumination for health and well-being may be counterproductive or harmful.
Lighting design should aim for higher corneal illuminance (Eeye) in architectural environments to better support human health.

Circadian Stimulus (CS) is best restricted to windowless environments (e.g., industrial control rooms, nursing bases) where staff spend long periods and work unsocial hours, rather than being a universal metric for all environments.
Future work should include longer-term studies and a wider range of environments, including those specifically designed for circadian needs.

tables.description: Circadian Stimulus (CS) and cubic illuminances (lx) for nine settings under overcast sky conditions.
key_stats: Ex values range from 123 lx to 7980 lx

tables.description: Circadian Stimulus (CS) and cubic illuminances (lx) for nine settings under sunny sky conditions.

limitations: Investigated a finite number of natural and built lit environments, not representing the true diversity of lit environments in contemporary life.
Captured only a momentary snapshot of the visual field during two daylight conditions, unable to describe full variation over time.
Possible technical drawbacks of the measuring equipment used, with spectrophotometer software excluding information on metric calculation and unconfirmed cosine correction.
Fundamental contradiction in using light metrics for precise physical measurement vs. approximating human response, especially for non-image forming functions.
Research in the field of human biology and light's role in health and well-being is still in its infancy.

paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: The beneficial effects of light on human non-image forming processes are subject to much research interest and are outlined in this article. Known mechanisms of impact include those on the circadian timing system, the arousal system and the affective system. An indication is made that it is important to consider the characteristics of the light field not just the light source when making recommendations concerning light of certain spectral quality. What types of light field are people exposed to on a regular basis and can these lit environments be considered beneficial? How much do these lit scenes differ in terms of spectral composition, as well as in light distribution patterns and illuminance levels, from those conditions that are currently suggested for optimising occupant health and wellbeing? A representative set of natural and built lit environments were identified ranging from seascapes/landscapes to an urban square and various interior architectural environments. A photometric and colorimetric snapshot was measured during the midday hours, to replicate the visual field as viewed from the perspective of the observer. The measured spectral irradiance of light received at the cornea was converted into derived lighting metrics that are the subject of current recommendation: relative sensitivity curve ( V λ), vertical/horizontal illuminance ratio ( Ev/Eh), cylindrical illuminance ( Ec) and circadian stimulus. The data were analysed to demonstrate that the indications are that more natural lit environments are expected to be beneficial. Discussion follows about the relative importance of spectral composition, intensity and light distribution within the visual field and how these might combine to optimise our health and wellbeing.  Practical application: Architectural and engineering designers are being encouraged to devise environments that promote human health and wellbeing. New lighting metrics are being suggested and this article seeks to indicate how effective these metrics are in their ability to characterise these lit environments.
